back: Removal of the waste products of metabolism, toxic substances and substances in excess.
notes: Not egestion, which removes undigested food.

front: What do the lungs and kidneys excrete?
back: Lungs: carbon dioxide. Kidneys: urea, excess water and excess ions.
notes: ZIMSEC: the skin excretes water, salts and a little urea in sweat.

front: Path of urine through the urinary system?
Regions of a kidney seen in section?
back: Outer cortex, inner medulla and (ZIMSEC) the pelvis where urine collects.
Blood at high pressure is filtered: water, glucose, urea and ions pass into the capsule; cells and proteins stay in the blood.
All of the glucose, some of the ions and most of the water.
Removal of the nitrogen-containing part of excess amino acids in the liver, forming urea.
It is toxic and would damage cells if it built up in the blood.

front: (ZIMSEC) How do the kidneys respond to dehydration?
back: They reabsorb more water, producing a small volume of concentrated urine (osmoregulation).

front: (ZIMSEC) How does dialysis remove urea but keep glucose?
back: Fluid has normal glucose and ion concentrations but no urea, so urea diffuses out through the membrane and glucose does not.
